Let\'s connect your Mac
Open Bridgey on your Mac, on the same Wi-Fi. It shows up below.
Paired with your Mac
Paired with %1$s
Do you want to copy on one device and paste on the other?
Text and links you copy move between this phone and your Mac.
Copy and paste between devices
Yes, automatically
Copy here, paste there. Nothing to tap.
Only when I tap Send
Send what you copied with one tap, from the app or the tile.
Should images and files copy too?
Big items move only when you paste, so copying stays quick.
Images and files on the clipboard
Yes, images and files too
Only text
Send your latest screenshot when you tap Send?
If you took a screenshot in the last minute, Send copied item sends it to your Mac.
Send a fresh screenshot
Do you want your phone\'s notifications on your Mac?
Messages and alerts from this phone show up on your Mac too.
Phone notifications on your Mac
Which apps already have a Mac app you use, like WhatsApp?
Bridgey keeps their notifications on this phone, so they don\'t show up twice on your Mac.
Kept on this phone
None of these
Do you want codes from text messages shown on your Mac?
Android hides one-time codes from other apps until this phone is linked to your Mac. Your Mac reads them on the Mac or in the cloud, as you choose there.
Codes from messages on your Mac
Yes, link my Mac
Should Bridgey tell you when something arrives from your Mac?
Files, links and calls from your Mac show as notifications on this phone.
Bridgey\'s own notifications
Do you take calls on your Mac?
See who\'s calling on your Mac, and answer or decline from there.
Phone calls on your Mac
Yes, answer and decline on my Mac
Your Mac can also start calls through this phone.
Just show who\'s calling
You answer on this phone.
Do you want to send files and photos between your phone and Mac?
Share or drop them, and they land on the other device.
Sending files and photos
Can your Mac look through this phone\'s files and photos?
Your Mac can list and download them. You choose if it may change anything.
Your Mac can browse this phone
Yes, just look
Your Mac sees and downloads, and changes nothing.
Yes, and let it change files
Your Mac may also upload and replace files here.
When you send a folder to your phone, where should it go?
Folders keep their structure either way.
Folders sent to this phone
I pick on my Mac while sending
Ask me on this phone each time
Always to my default folder
Do you want to control your Mac from your phone, like a touchpad or a slide clicker?
Your Mac has to allow this phone too. You can stop at any time.
Control your Mac from this phone
Use the volume keys to change slides?
While the slides remote is open, volume down goes to the next slide and volume up to the previous one.
Volume keys change slides
Lock, sleep and volume from your phone?
Quick buttons for your Mac. Your Mac decides what this phone may do.
Lock, sleep and volume for your Mac
Control music on your Mac from your phone?
Play, pause and skip what\'s playing on your Mac.
Music controls for your Mac
Take photos for your Mac with your phone?
Your Mac asks, you take the photo here, and it lands on your Mac.
Photos for your Mac
Keep Do Not Disturb in step on both devices?
When one goes quiet, the other follows. Give the same answer on your Mac.
Do Not Disturb in step
Yes, both ways
Only this phone follows my Mac
Only my Mac follows this phone
Open links from one device on the other?
Share a link to your Mac and it opens in the browser there.
Open links on the other device
Ring a device when you can\'t find it?
Ring this phone from your Mac, or your Mac from here. A short ping works too.
Find and ping your devices
Show this phone\'s battery on your Mac?
Both devices share their battery level.
Battery level on both devices
Can Bridgey keep connection stats to help fix problems?
They stay on this phone, without message or file contents, and leave only if you export them.
Connection stats on this phone
Show previews of what you copied in the activity list?
Off shows only what happened, like Text copied.
Previews in activity
How new do you want updates?
Newer builds get features sooner, with more rough edges.
Updates
Steady
Stable: tested releases. Best for most people.
Early
Beta: new features before they reach Stable.
Newest every day
Nightly: built from every change. Expect rough edges.
Should Bridgey keep working when your phone is locked?
Phones stop apps in the background to save battery. Allowing Bridgey keeps your Mac connected.
Keeps working in the background
Keep Wi-Fi awake while your Mac is connected?
Fewer drops on phones that slow Wi-Fi down when the screen is off, at some battery cost.
Wi-Fi stays awake while connected
Do you prefer less motion on screen?
Screens fade instead of sliding, and nothing bounces.
Less motion
Yes, less motion
No, keep it
